grand_strategy.reading: Chad's grand strategy is the survival of the Déby regime on borders it cannot seal: Sudan's war, the Libyan east and the Lake Chad jihadists all press on one army. Having lost France as guarantor, N'Djamena spreads its patronage across Abu Dhabi, Moscow, Budapest and Haftar, and buys access more than protection. The gaps are the Zaghawa question (the clan's Darfur kin among the RSF's victims, a reading taken from the SDN card and not sourced here), the oil corridor, the Central African Republic, Cameroon and the United States, none yet sourced for this card.

stances.note: Chad's side of the rivalry: N'Djamena expelled four Sudanese diplomats (mid-Dec 2023), and on 23 Feb 2026 closed the eastern border indefinitely, citing Sudanese armed groups after fighting at al-Tina. Khartoum's complaint of Nov 2024 accuses Chad of aiding the RSF; Chad does not accept it. Rival: friction and mutual blame, no declared aim to destroy the other state. Mirror of the SDN card (rival, cooling, bond none), same sources. Trend cooling because the border closure is the latest step. Bond none. Gap: Chad's own statement on the RSF accusation is not found.
